title: After Dinosaurs Died, a Massive Fungus Inherited the Forests - Nautilus
gist: Chinese mycologists described a large new ascomycete fungus, nicknamed D. rex, found near the roots of Chinese cork oaks. Only about 200,000 of an estimated 2-6 million fungal species are identified.

insights.claim: Of an estimated 2-6 million fungal species on Earth only around 200,000 have been identified, because most fungal biomass is unseen mycelial networks.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Vast undescribed biodiversity suggests untapped biological and biotech discovery space.
insights.locator: of the estimated 2-6 million species of fungi

insights.claim: Chinese mycologists discovered a new large fungal species after noticing sizable whitish fruiting bodies near the roots of Chinese cork oaks in both subtropical and temperate forests.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Illustrates ongoing discovery of large new species in well-studied regions.

insights.claim: The new fungus appears to belong to ascomycota, the largest fungal phylum, which releases spores from sacs rather than producing mushrooms.
